companyIntro.name: Nimbus Digital

projectBackground.name: Fintra Payments — Refund Workflow
projectBackground.context: Support wants 'a better refund process'. Developers say the request is too vague to estimate.

manager.name: Julia Hoffmann
manager.note: Developers can't build 'better'. Give them behaviours they can test.

assignment.title: Clarify and prioritise the refund workflow
assignment.brief: Rewrite vague requirements, define acceptance criteria, apply MoSCoW and forecast delivery.

documents.name: Backlog Summary
documents.note: 20 stories totalling 120 story points; team velocity 30 points per sprint.

tasks.title: Vague Requirement
tasks.prompt: 'The system should be fast and user-friendly.' What's wrong?
tasks.reasoning: Requirements must be specific enough to verify.
tasks.mistake: Untestable requirements cause disputes at acceptance.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Acceptance Criteria
options: Given a paid order, when support issues a refund, then the customer receives a confirmation email within 5 minutes
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: MoSCoW Limit
tasks.prompt: With 20 stories and a 60% cap on Must-haves, what is the maximum number of Must stories?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Delivery Forecast
tasks.prompt: The backlog is 120 points and velocity is 30 points per sprint. How many sprints are needed?
tasks.mistake: Optimistic velocity guesses cause missed dates.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Elicitation Techniques
tasks.prompt: Select techniques suitable for clarifying the refund process.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: User Story
tasks.prompt: Write one user story with two acceptance criteria for the refund workflow.
tasks.modelAnswer: As a support agent, I want to issue a full refund for a paid order so that customers are reimbursed without a developer's help. Acceptance: Given a paid order, when I choose full refund, then the payment is reversed and the order status shows Refunded. Given a refund, when it completes, then the customer receives a confirmation email within 5 minutes.
tasks.reasoning: A good story has role, goal, benefit and testable criteria.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Feature Nobody Wanted
caseStudy.background: A team built a reporting feature from one manager's request. Usage after launch was 3% because the actual users were never interviewed.
caseStudy.challenges: One stakeholder spoke for all users.
questions: Why was one stakeholder not enough?
caseStudy.solution: Nimbus added mandatory user interviews and a value hypothesis to each epic.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Validate with real users before building.

quiz.q: In the case study usage was low because:

prompts: How do you handle a stakeholder who wants everything?
Which technique do you trust most?
